headline: AI financing doubts keep markets cautious heading into Thanksgiving week
body: Equity markets are carrying a cautious, AI-skeptical tone into the holiday-shortened week after a choppy stretch in which optimism around easier Fed policy kept bumping against renewed doubts about artificial-intelligence spending. The Dow dropped roughly 560 points (about 1.1%) in the middle of last week and the S&P 500 slipped further the next session as the Nasdaq extended its slide, with coverage attributing the pressure to lingering unease over AI growth even though Nvidia's latest results and revenue guidance came in strong. That unease was reinforced by Anthropic's blockbuster Nasdaq debut — a roughly $1.5 trillion valuation that briefly topped SpaceX as the largest IPO on record — which popped sharply at the open before fading as investors zeroed in on AI companies' heavy debt loads and unclear paths to profitability.

Retail and social-media chatter offered little in the way of a fresh, confirmable signal today, so this read leans more on price action and headline flow than on any specific wave of trader sentiment; the one recurring theme in recent commentary is that retail positioning has generally tilted toward calls rather than downside hedges, suggesting the dip-buying instinct hasn't disappeared even as the broader mood has cooled. Combined with a Federal Reserve whose December rate-cut odds remain unsettled and a market still digesting whether the AI buildout can justify its financing, the overall posture looks like cautious hesitation rather than outright risk-off capitulation — participants trimming enthusiasm at the margins while waiting for more economic data and earnings to clarify the picture.
